newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan PM vows to improve troubled ties with China.
newsitem.headline: Japan PM vows to improve troubled ties with China.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Friday his new government would place a priority on improving strained relations between Tokyo and Beijing.
"I would like to have a close dialogue with China and strengthen bilateral relations," Hashimoto told a news conference, the first since his re-election on Thursday.

Japanese officials said Sino-Japanese ties have hit their lowest point since normalisation of relations in 1978 because of a bitter dispute over Japanese-controlled islands in the East China Sea. The islands, called the Senkakus in Japanese and Diaoyus in Chinese, are also claimed by Taiwan.
A Japanese right-wing group built a lighthouse on one of the islands in July, triggering anti-Japanese demonstrations in Hong Kong and Taiwan.
Hashimoto himself caused a furore that same month when he visited the controversial Yasukuni Shrine which honours Japanese war dead.
"In parallel to Japan-U.S. relations, we must stabilise and promote Sino-Japanese relations," Hashimoto said.
"That is important not only for the two countries but also for the Asia-Pacific region and the international community," he added.
Hashimoto suggested that Tokyo might even soon resume grant aid to China.
Japan froze the aid, worth about seven billion yen ($62.5 million) in August 1995 as a mainly symbolic protest at China's nuclear test programme.
The bulk of Japanese aid to China, about 580 billion yen ($5.17 billion) in yen loans over the next three years, has not been affected by the nuclear testing.
Last month, China signed the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty at the United Nations and imposed a moratorium on future nuclear testing.
"I have no intention of saying we should scrap grant-in-aid," Hashimoto said.
